openai.feedback:
- Category: bug
- Severity: medium
- File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/lib/git_side_release.py:66
- Finding: A token containing invalid UTF-8 makes `read_text()` raise `UnicodeDecodeError`, which the `except OSError` does not catch. The token remains on disk, and `main()` fails open before measuring coverage. Consequently, every subsequent below-threshold commit is allowed until someone removes the token, violating AC-7’s every-run removal and normal-evaluation fallback.
- Suggestion: Treat decoding failures as an invalid token and ensure the token is removed before returning to normal coverage evaluation. Add a test with invalid UTF-8 token bytes that verifies the commit blocks and the token disappears.

The implementation otherwise follows the specified design, with substantial behavioral coverage. Ship-with-fixes: correct malformed-token handling before merging; workspace inspection and test execution were unavailable because command execution was blocked by policy.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

glm.feedback:
## Findings

- Category: test
  Severity: medium
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/tests/test_git_precommit_rtm_coverage.py:186-191 (`test_anti_ratchet_step_and_coverage_step_are_both_wired`)
  Finding: AC-8's "both always run; no early exit skips the second step when the bloat baseline is absent" is verified only by substring/index checks on the hook's text. A `pre-commit` that early-exits (e.g., `exit 0` after step 1, or an `exit` inside the baseline branch) would still pass this test, because the test never asserts the substring ordering captures control flow. There is no behavioral test where the bloat baseline is absent AND the manifest is below threshold, asserting the commit is blocked.
  Suggestion: Add a test that removes/never creates `shipwright_bloat_baseline.json` in the temp repo, stages a 1/2 manifest, and asserts `commit` is blocked with `BLOCKED` — that proves the coverage step runs when step 1's guard is false.

- Category: test
  Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/tests/test_git_precommit_rtm_coverage.py (file level)
  Finding: AC-8's "uv missing" branches (anti-ratchet blocks; coverage WARNs and does not run) have no test at all — not even for the coverage WARN branch, which is pure shell and easily exercised by putting a `uv`-less stub dir first on PATH in `hook_env`.
  Suggestion: Add a subprocess test with a PATH that excludes `uv`, asserting exit != 0, the anti-ratchet message, and the coverage `WARN ... NOT evaluating`.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: medium
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/hooks/git_precommit_rtm_coverage.py:62-72 (`_project_root`) and plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/hooks/check_rtm_coverage.py:263-270
  Finding: The token is granted at `project_root` as resolved by the PreToolUse hook (which, per the plan review's finding 5, may consult the session env) but claimed at `_project_root(...)` resolved with `allow_env=False`. If the two resolutions ever disagree (session env pointing at a different managed root), `grant` writes and `claim` reads different files and the hand-off silently degrades to "no token" — the operator is asked for a second override with no diagnostic. Both `claim`'s `(False, None)` and the code path make this indistinguishable from "no release ever happened."
  Suggestion: Either resolve both sides with the same `allow_env=False` policy in the grant path, or emit a distinguishable WARN when a token exists under the toplevel but not under the resolved project root.

- Category: bug
  Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/hooks/check_rtm_coverage.py:263-269
  Finding: In `_block`'s release path, `import git_side_release` and `grant()` are outside any try/except. `grant` catches `OSError` internally, but an `ImportError` (lib path wrong, filesystem issue) or any unexpected exception propagates out of `_block` and can turn an already-consumed override release into a hook crash/block — the opposite of the fail-open posture everywhere else in this change.
  Suggestion: Wrap the import + grant in `try/except Exception` and fold the message into `lost`.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/lib/git_side_release.py:66-70 (`claim`)
  Finding: When `age < -CLOCK_SKEW_S` (mtime far in the future, e.g., a clock step back after grant), the expired-token message reports `released this command -N s ago ... hand-off lasts 120 s`, which is nonsense output and mildly misattributes the failure. Also, the stale-token sweep only happens when the token is read; a token left by a crash before `claim` (e.g., import failure in `check()`) persists until the next successful run — within the 2-minute TTL, so bounded, but worth noting the "removed by EVERY git-side run" claim in AC-7 has this exception.
  Suggestion: Clamp the reported age (`max(age, 0)`) or use a distinct sentence for future-stamped tokens.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/hooks/git_precommit_rtm_coverage.py:96-99
  Finding: When the hand-off token was claimed, the git-side check skips `override.try_release` entirely and returns 0 with only a stderr WARN — but it does not print the measured figure on the allow path (the at/above-threshold path does). Minor inconsistency with AC-2's "output carries the one-line figure" spirit; not an AC violation since AC-2 covers only the threshold case.
  Suggestion: Include `reason` (the figure) in the released WARN line — it already does via `reason`, so this is satisfied; no change needed if `describe(measure)` is in `reason`. Verify `reason` is populated before the handoff branch (it is). Withdraw if confirmed.

(Correction on the last item: `reason` is built before the handoff branch and included in the WARN, so no defect there.)

## Other checks

- Security: no injection, secret, or authorization issues. Token path is derived from a constant hook name; `subprocess` calls use argument lists, no shell interpolation.
- AC-1..AC-7 and AC-9 each map to real end-to-end tests that run actual `git commit` with the real hook; the fake-framework tests for exit-code-3-only blocking, missing script, and interpreter failure are behaviorally sound (a regression to "any non-zero blocks" would fail them).
- The `pre-commit` rewrite correctly preserves prior anti-ratchet behavior (exit non-zero on uv-missing or check failure) while removing `set -e` in favor of an explicit `status` accumulator — no regression to existing callers visible.
- `.gitattributes` LF pinning for hook scripts is a correct mitigation for the autocrlf fail-open concern.

Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes — the implementation is sound and the ACs are genuinely tested end-to-end; the concrete gaps are the text-only AC-8 wiring test, the untested uv-missing branch, and the small fail-open hole in the grant path. All are contained fixes.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
